strengths.text: Its explanation is exact: the score is a sum over seed labels, so nothing is approximated.
Seed contribution and Leave-one-seed-out are faithful: removing the inputs flagged as important really does move the score.

weaknesses.text: Barely better than guessing: test AUC 0.499 (0.5 is a coin flip).
For trolls, 59% of the top-3 seed labels behind the score come from the troll's own ring.

checklist.text: Test on data collected after your training data. Behaviour drifts, and a validation split from the same period hides that.
Choose the decision threshold on held-out data for the precision you need; a wrongly banned real user costs more than a missed bot.
Keep a fixed audit sample of labelled accounts and re-run the explanations on it after every retrain.
List which inputs an attacker can change cheaply (posting rate, hashtags, timing) and test the model with those changed.
Do not deploy as a detector. At this accuracy it flags real users about as often as fakes.
checklist.because: Barely better than guessing: test AUC 0.499 (0.5 is a coin flip).
